Resolves #19684

A Group projection no longer reconciles over a newer commit's document. The Group dispatches a projection only while its snapshot is current, but the projection runs when the participant's refresh chain reaches it. When that chain is behind, a later commit may already have adopted the participant's next document. In the Workstation's undo of a popup's native close, main's return projection ran about a second late, after the reopened popup had adopted the pane under the undo. It took the live pane back, and the undo's own projection then removed it from main, so the pane ended up in neither window. The diagnosis, from hosted probes that tag every projection with a sequence id, is on #19684.
- `WorkspaceSet`'s adapter hands each Group projection an `isCurrent()` check over the participant's revision, and `projectDockCommit()` passes it to the refresh.
- `refreshDockWorkspace()` stops a superseded projection at each boundary where it already stops for a destroyed workspace: after the host mounts, after the FLIP capture, and after the reveal-pane releases. A stale document therefore causes no capture, hook or release either.
- Direct `projectDockZoneDocument()` callers pass no check. They keep the pinned contract that two projections issued in one tick both run.

Evidence: L2 (unit arms through a real Group that go red without the fix, one per guard; the full unit suite; a hosted A/B of the e2e journey) → L3 required for the ten-shard `dev` receipt. Residual: that receipt. Residual-Owner: #19657.

## AC Evidence
| AC | Evidence |
|---|---|
| AC-1 | #19684's body: hosted runs 38324514355 and 38325733035 name the ordering. Main's stale return projection resolves `commits` out of the popup after the popup adopted it. |
| AC-2 | `DockWorkspace.spec.mjs`, "projectDockCommit — a projection the chain reaches after a newer commit stands down". Two participants of one Group share a live pane, and main's return projection waits while the undo commits on both: queued behind a busy chain, inside its FLIP capture, or inside its reveal-pane releases. Without the fix, all three go red: main takes the pane, or the stale document reaches the FLIP capture or the pre-refresh hook. A newer write the popup refuses after main adopted it leaves main's owed projection to land. |
| AC-3 | [Hosted run 38327801858](https://github.com/neomjs/neo/actions/runs/38327801858), from a temporary branch carrying the first commit, a spec hook and its workflow. Four interleaved rounds on one runner each run `:2604` five times on `dev`'s `Workspace.mjs` and five times on this one. After the undo, the hook awaits main's refresh chain and checks where the pane is. On `dev`, 17 of 20 runs passed the assertion, yet the pane ended outside the popup in 19 of 20: the assertion usually saw it before main's stale projection took it. With the fix, 20 of 20 passed and the pane stayed in the popup in all 20. |

## Deltas from ticket
The ticket proposed the stand-down inside `projectDockZoneDocument()`'s chained refresh, for every caller. That would drop the first of two direct projections issued in one tick, which the arm "projectDockZoneDocument SERIALIZES" pins as "serialized, not dropped". Direct callers also chain follow-ups, such as focus, onto their own commit's promise. The check therefore applies only to Group projections. It compares the participant's revision, which the adapter already keeps: a successful adoption advances it, while a failed write's compensation restores both the document, as a clone, and the revision. Neither the document reference nor the snapshot can serve, since compensation clones the one and a commit to a sibling replaces the other.

size-guard-growth: src/dashboard/dock/Workspace.mjs — the fence adds two code lines beside the refresh's existing destroyed-guards, the one place a running projection can stop; `dev` sat at the 1,000-line target, so the file is enrolled at 1,002

## Test Evidence
- Mutations, each reverted afterwards:
  - the first commit's reference fence: only the compensation arm goes red (`built` is `[]`, not `[true]`);
  - a check that is always current: the four supersession arms go red; always superseded: all six;
  - without the after-mount check, the busy-chain arm goes red (the stale document reaches the FLIP capture);
  - without the after-FLIP check, the FLIP arm goes red (it reaches the pre-refresh hook);
  - without the post-release check, the release arm goes red (main takes the pane).
- `npm run test-unit`: 5056 passed, 2 skipped. The serialization arm stays green.
